notes: Region 1 holds a faint, broken stamp impression, illegible in both orientations. Region 2 is the roll number in pencil; the leader label (region 4) reads WELTE-MIGNON No. 3333, Piano-Concert E major, 1st movement, Fr. Liszt. Regions 3 and 4 carry a modern English pencil note about repair, ending 28 April 2002; not a punch date.

Six-figure stamp in black ink, every figure plain: 8 1 1 0 2 5. Read as day-month-year it gives day 81, which is impossible, so the day is not recoverable. If the last four figures are month and year, as on other stamped rolls in this batch, the month is October and the year 1925. 3335 is written in pencil on region 4; region 3 holds only a smudge.
Six-figure stamp in black ink, all figures plain. Day 29 forces the day-month-year order.
Pencil, separators dropped, read as 8.2.23. Region 6 carries 3357 in the same hand, which is the roll number. Regions 1, 2, 4 and 5 hold no writing.

Pencil, separators dropped, 26.5.22; day 26 forces the order. The leader label (region 4) reads WELTE-MIGNON No. 3376, Die Jüdin, F. Halévy, gespielt von Dr. Berend, so 26522 is not the catalogue number.

Pencil, four figures, read as 5.2.20. 3398 is written on region 2 and printed on the leader label (Naïla-Walzer, L. Delibes, Bearbeitung von Ernst von Dohnányi, gespielt von Alfred Grünfeld), so 5220 is not the catalogue number. Region 3 holds only brush marks.
Pencil, separators dropped. The middle figure is either 9 or 2, so the date is 11.9.22 or 11.2.22; the day 11 and the year 1922 are clear. Region 2 holds only a degraded line of specks.
Pencil, separators dropped, 13.2.22. The three closing figures are consistent twos.
